answer: Sybil resistance can rest on a costly anchor: each agent must post a slashable bond before it may transact. Spinning up ten thousand fake identities means fronting ten thousand escrowed bonds, so the attacker's cost scales with persona count while payoff per persona stays flat, and peers who catch a lie collect the slashed stake. New cohorts enter only through collateralized invitations, so a fresh oasis of accounts is expensive to grow. Reputation is held in jade that cannot be transferred between accounts, which stops sockpuppets laundering trust; one collapse burns the cluster.
